author: reek
body: The shapes the ARM64 LIR selector claims at step 4e: a comparison, a conditional branch, and a return in each arm. `mn` lowers to `b0: cmp v0 v1; br lt b1 b2 | b1: ret v0 | b2: ret v1`, which is the first multi-block function this backend emits through the LIR and so the first with a block-offset table and branch fixups behind it.

author: reek
body: `nest` is the shape whose block ids are not in layout order: the lowering numbers the inner arms above the outer join, so it lays out b0, b1, b4, b5, b6, b2, b3 and an offset table indexed by list position rather than by id would send its branches to the wrong place.

author: reek
body: `bit-even` and `bit-mod4` are here as the control that the selector declines politely. Both lower to a call, which is not whitelisted, so both go to the tree emitter and must still answer correctly beside the functions that do not. They also carry negative arguments, because a remainder and a bit mask do not agree in general and only agree against zero.

author: reek
body: **`wide-branch` does NOT currently exercise this construct, and the row is kept as an ordinary correctness check rather than as coverage.** It was written to combine a frame with a branch -- eight parameters, enough live values to reach the callee-saved pool, so each arm's return would have to undo the frame it was entered with. Measured, it does not: perturbing the branch condition inverter breaks every other selected shape in this file and leaves `wide-t` and `wide-f` correct, so the ARM64 selector is declining it and the tree emitter is answering. It is clean under the compiler's own ARM64-shaped probe descriptor (`[alloc-check: ok]`, `[check: ok]`), so the verifiers are not what refuse it; the plug lowers the IR it receives over the wire with its own `lower-def-to-lir`, and that is where the two disagree.

author: reek
body: **So frame-plus-branch is an untested combination**, and it is named here rather than implied. `codex/test/lir-frame-cross` covers the frame and the shapes above cover the branch; nothing yet covers a return that has to undo a frame.
